transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, what brought me in is that... I guess things just got really out of hand recently. I went from being a normal landscaping crew guy to suddenly trying to run three different bids at once. I was calling city people, lining up plant suppliers, and messaging everybody I knew about this big park idea I had. It was just like I couldn't shut it off.
During that time when you were working on these bids, did you feel like you had special powers, or did you see or hear things that others around you did not?

No, nothing like that. I didn't think I had, like, superpowers or anything. I just... I just felt really confident, I guess. Like I was finally stepping up and doing big things, and I had all the energy to do it. 

And no, I definitely wasn't seeing or hearing anything that wasn't there. I was just really wired and focused on all those projects.
Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt extremely low, hopeless, or lost interest in your usual activities for two weeks or longer?

Yeah, I have. Actually, that's kind of where I'm at right now, to be honest. It's been going on for a while, definitely more than two weeks. I just feel really... empty, I guess. 

I used to love getting out in the woods to clear my head. I'd go hiking, take pictures of creek beds and trees, try to catch the light just right. But lately... I don't know. I just leave the camera in the truck. I don't care if the light is perfect or not. I just don't have the energy or the interest to do any of it anymore. It's like someone just turned the volume all the way down on everything I used to enjoy.
During these periods when you feel very low and hopeless, have you ever felt like you were losing touch with reality, or heard or seen things that others could not?

No, I haven't. Even when I'm feeling this down, I've never heard voices or seen anything that wasn't there. I just feel really, really low, but I know what's real and what's not. I'm just tired and don't care about much, but I'm not losing touch with reality.
During that period when you were so wired and focused on those landscaping projects, did your behavior become so disruptive that you were unable to work or had to be hospitalized?

No, I didn't have to go to the hospital or anything like that. I was actually working the whole time. I mean... I was probably working *too* much, putting in crazy hours on all those bids and jobs. But I was still getting the work done. It didn't stop me from working, and I definitely wasn't hospitalized. I was just... really intense about getting it all finished.

During that time when you were working those long hours and calling everyone, did your friends, family, or coworkers comment that you were acting differently or that your behavior was unusual for you?

Yeah, they did. My crew definitely noticed. A couple of the guys told me I needed to slow down, that I was talking too fast and jumping from one idea to the next without finishing the first one. My sister actually came over one night and asked if I was on something, just because I couldn't sit still and was going on and on about expanding the business to three different counties. So, yeah, people definitely noticed I wasn't acting like my usual self.
How many days in a row would you say you were feeling that intense, wired energy and working those long hours?

It was about two weeks. That whole... fired-up, overconfident stretch started right when I began remaking myself for this big park pitch. I just kept going non-stop like that for around fourteen days straight, and then I completely crashed.
